prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent modular sprite sheet for an existing retro 16px-grid tactical RPG. The two attached atlases are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY; generate NEW COMPLETE environment buildings, no change to those atlases. Match their humble low-saturation hand-pixelled 16-bit Fire Emblem Gaiden-inspired overhead/slightly frontal view, mauve grey stone, moss olive, straw and weathered brown wood, gently textured compact clusters. No sharp modern game style, no vector smooth edges, no isometric diamonds. Make ONE clean sheet of TWELVE DISTINCT WHOLE objects in a strict 4 columns by 3 rows arrangement with generous transparent separation. Each object stands entirely inside its cell with transparent padding, never clipped. Row1: (1) massive weathered coastal castle keep with THREE unequal tall towers, broken battlements, sea-weathered masonry and moss, very recognizable fortress silhouette, open entrance at bottom; (2) ruined round watchtower, exposed broken top and climbing ivy; (3) heavy paired stone sea-gate bastions with an OPEN central arch and weathered crenels; (4) tiered cliff outcrop with grass cap and stony sea-worn face. Row2: (1) timber granary on stone footing with exterior sacks, (2) thatched village clinic with hanging pale cloth, no text, (3) canvas military command pavilion with spears stacked alongside, (4) large timber-braced dark mine entrance cut into uneven rock, mine cart at side. Row3: (1) waterfront warehouse with slate roof and small crane, (2) fishing cottage with net rack and baskets, (3) low ruined fortress wall with a jagged breach and rubble, (4) weathered ancient causeway arch ruin with broken upper stones. Whole objects intended to be normalized for 64-112 native pixel sprites; keep every object chunky and readable with clear silhouettes, crisp actual pixel clusters and limited palettes, rather than high-resolution painted miniatures. Transparent background, no terrain rectangles, no cast drop-shadow outside sprites, no text, labels, grid lines, UI, characters, weapons in use, or watermark. Atlas refs are only palette/material/perspective support. Make twelve complete reusable game sprites.
module_normalization: Whole silhouettes cropped with padding, proportionally normalized to native footprints using nearest-neighbour, original alpha retained, 48-color per module and lossless oxipng.
